title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: opening, funding and the unfunded closure
content:
## Policy clause

1. **Opening.** A new Savings & Money Market Accounts account opens in applied status with a zero balance and no automatic transfer.
2. **Age.** The customer's age in whole years on the opening date, taken from the date of birth on the customer profile, must be at least the tier's minimum age to open.
3. **Required checking.** For a tier that names a required checking tier (any value other than "none"), the customer must already hold an active checking account of one of the listed tiers on the opening date.
4. **Activation.** The account becomes active on the business day its first deposit posts, provided that deposit is at least the tier's minimum opening deposit. A smaller first deposit is returned and does not activate the account. On activation, the posted date of the opening deposit is recorded as the account's latest customer-initiated activity.
5. **Unfunded closure.** An account still in applied status is closed as unfunded once 30 calendar days have passed after the account was opened.
6. **Promotional end date.** For a tier that offers a promotional APY, the promotional end date is recorded at opening as the opening date plus the tier's promotional period in calendar months, falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist in the month reached.

## Basis of decision

- **Authority.** The age test uses the date of birth held on the customer profile; the required-checking test uses the bank's checking account records for the same customer; the unfunded-closure test uses the opening date on the savings account record. Each is read from the system record before the action; a customer's statement of age or holdings does not replace it.
- **Object correlation.** The required checking account must belong to the same customer who opens the savings account.

## How the 30-day funding window is counted

- The clock starts from the business event "the account was opened", evidenced by the account's opening date.
- Count calendar days with the day after the opening date as day 1.
- The unfunded closure is due when the current date is on or after the opening date plus 30 calendar days. Reaching that day exactly is enough (inclusive boundary).
- Calendar days are counted, not 24-hour periods and not business days.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| Opening date | Current date | Day number | Account still applied? | Unfunded closure due? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 March | 30 March | day 29 | yes | no |
| 1 March | 31 March | day 30 | yes | yes |
| 1 March | 31 March | day 30 | no, activated on 20 March | no; the account is not in applied status |

## Activation checklist

| First deposit versus the tier's minimum opening deposit | Result |
|---|---|
| at least the minimum | account becomes active on the business day the deposit posts |
| below the minimum | deposit returned; account stays in applied status |

## Promotional end date: month-end example (hypothetical)

For an account opened on 31 August on a tier whose promotional period were 3 calendar months (an illustrative figure, not a tier value), 31 August plus 3 calendar months reaches 31 November, which does not exist, so the recorded end date falls back to 30 November.

## Points of judgement

**The customer turns the tier's minimum age the day after the opening date. Does the age test pass on the opening date?** No; age is taken in whole years on the opening date itself.

**A customer requests a tier that names a required checking tier but holds only an active checking account of a tier not on that list. Does the required-checking test pass?** No; only an active account of one of the listed checking tiers satisfies it.
